item.text: {"chapter_id":"8B","shard_id":"8B-S04","reviewed_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0018-E016","BATCH-0018-E017","BATCH-0018-E018","BATCH-0018-E019","BATCH-0021-R01-E012","BATCH-0024-E001","BATCH-0024-E002","BATCH-0024-E004","BATCH-0024-E005","BATCH-0024-E007","BATCH-0024-E008","BATCH-0026-E002","BATCH-0026-E003","BATCH-0026-E004","BATCH-0026-E005","BATCH-0026-E006","BATCH-0026-E007","BATCH-0026-E008","BATCH-0026-E009","BATCH-0026-E010","BATCH-0026-E011","BATCH-0026-E012","BATCH-0026-E014","BATCH-0026-E016","BATCH-0026-E017","BATCH-0026-E020","BATCH-0026-E022","BATCH-0028-E003","BATCH-0028-E004","BATCH-0028-E005","BATCH-0028-E006","BATCH-0028-E007","BATCH-0029-E002","BATCH-0029-E003","BATCH-0029-E004","BATCH-0029-E005","BATCH-0029-E007","BATCH-0029-E009","BATCH-0029-E010","BATCH-0030-E002","BATCH-0030-E003","BATCH-0030-E004","BATCH-0030-E005","BATCH-0030-E006","BATCH-0030-E007","BATCH-0030-E008","BATCH-0030-E011","BATCH-0030-E012","BATCH-0031-E002","BATCH-0031-E003","BATCH-0031-E004","BATCH-0031-E006","BATCH-0031-E008","BATCH-0031-E012","BATCH-0031-E013","BATCH-0031-E014","BATCH-0031-E015","BATCH-0031-E016","BATCH-0031-E017","BATCH-0031-E018","BATCH-0031-E019","BATCH-0032-E001"],"answers":[{"question_id":"8B.1","answer":"The shard documents a clear, mostly explicit program: republican austerity and anti-corruption; poverty and social-policy expansion; security pacification and a proposed gradual military withdrawal; energy and food self-sufficiency; state-led infrastructure; migrant protection; and stronger state control in strategic sectors. The program was expressed in campaign platforms, presidential speeches, party documents, and later 2023 reform proposals. Some priorities evolved or conflicted with earlier commitments, particularly demilitarization versus expanded military roles.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0024-E001","BATCH-0024-E007","BATCH-0024-E005","BATCH-0029-E005","BATCH-0030-E007","BATCH-0031-E004"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0026-E010","BATCH-0026-E022","BATCH-0031-E012"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Most program evidence predates 2023; the shard does not provide a complete dated 2023 strategic document or a consolidated hierarchy among competing goals."]},{"question_id":"8B.2","answer":"There is substantial evidence of translating priorities into laws, institutions, budgets, appointments, and directives: the National Guard, social-rights and labor reforms, pensions and social programs, energy initiatives, military control of infrastructure, and 2023 proposals concerning judicial and autonomous institutions. Translation was inconsistent: several institutions were left without commissioners, forensic and archival commitments remained incomplete, and some initiatives conflicted with constitutional or judicial constraints.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0024-E008","BATCH-0026-E005","BATCH-0026-E014","BATCH-0026-E020","BATCH-0029-E007","BATCH-0030-E007","BATCH-0031-E008","BATCH-0031-E013"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0018-E017","BATCH-0018-E019","BATCH-0028-E003","BATCH-0030-E005","BATCH-0031-E004"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Several cited reforms are described through analytical or advocacy sources, and the shard does not provide a complete legislative, budgetary, or appointment record for all program components."]},{"question_id":"8B.3","answer":"The shard shows strong mobilization of presidential, party, administrative, and military networks toward selected priorities. The administration redirected substantial resources, expanded social-program spending, created and used Morena machinery, and assigned the armed forces security, infrastructure, ports, airports, customs, banking, and rail functions. Mobilization was materially weakened by opaque reallocations, limited civilian capacity, incomplete coordination, and disputed fiscal controls.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0026-E005","BATCH-0026-E006","BATCH-0026-E022","BATCH-0029-E007","BATCH-0030-E007","BATCH-0031-E013","BATCH-0031-E015"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0018-E019","BATCH-0030-E006","BATCH-0030-E011"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The shard contains little direct administrative documentation linking each expenditure or deployment to a specific frozen objective, and some resource figures require unit verification."]},{"question_id":"8B.4","answer":"The ruler empowered loyal and disciplined implementers, especially military actors and close political allies, and used them to execute security, infrastructure, and social-program priorities. This produced organizational reach but raised capability and fit concerns: analysts describe loyalty being prioritized over technical competence, military personnel undertaking civilian functions without relevant experience, delayed autonomous-body appointments, and protection or retention of politically close figures despite alleged corruption concerns.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0026-E006","BATCH-0026-E022","BATCH-0028-E006","BATCH-0029-E007","BATCH-0031-E013","BATCH-0031-E015"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0026-E014","BATCH-0031-E004","BATCH-0030-E006"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The shard does not provide a comprehensive personnel roster, performance-based appointment record, or systematic evidence of replacement decisions across ministries."]},{"question_id":"8B.5","answer":"Coordination and reach were substantial in the presidential, party, military, and social-program networks, but uneven across civilian institutions and territories. The shard records nationwide military and infrastructure deployment, extensive party organization, and federal programs, alongside fragmented forensic coordination, nonfunctioning or impaired autonomous bodies, incomplete archive transfers, and military resistance to civilian investigative demands.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0018-E018","BATCH-0018-E019","BATCH-0026-E014","BATCH-0026-E020","BATCH-0029-E007","BATCH-0031-E013"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0030-E006","BATCH-0030-E011","BATCH-0031-E019"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Evidence is stronger for central initiatives and institutional conflicts than for routine compliance, milestone tracking, or territorial implementation across all regions."]},{"question_id":"8B.6","answer":"Many priorities became observable practice: minimum-wage increases, social transfers, labor-law changes, military administration of infrastructure and security, and partial opening of the Maya Train. However, implementation frequently remained incomplete or produced adverse operational evidence: forensic banks were not functioning, archives were withheld, the Maya Train opened partially with major delays and cost escalation, and some reforms were implemented through secrecy or contested procedures.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0018-E017","BATCH-0018-E019","BATCH-0030-E004","BATCH-0030-E005","BATCH-0031-E008","BATCH-0032-E001"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0030-E011","BATCH-0031-E002","BATCH-0031-E013"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The shard does not supply complete service-quality, enforcement, or project-performance audits for the full program portfolio."]},{"question_id":"8B.7","answer":"Results were mixed relative to the ruler's stated goals. Favorable movement included a 20% minimum-wage increase, lower measured multidimensional poverty by 2022, and evidence that social transfers reduced measured poverty. Adverse or unresolved outcomes included persistent or increased health-access deprivation, educational lag, weak growth, high homicide and disappearance levels, corruption concerns, infrastructure cost overruns, and distributional evidence that the poorest received a smaller share of social spending. Attribution is limited by the pandemic, inherited conditions, remittances, external trends, and the absence of causal evaluations.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0021-R01-E012","BATCH-0026-E002","BATCH-0026-E008","BATCH-0031-E008","BATCH-0031-E016","BATCH-0031-E018","BATCH-0032-E001"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0026-E002","BATCH-0029-E004","BATCH-0030-E004","BATCH-0031-E014","BATCH-0031-E015"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Many outcome measures are lagged, cumulative, national, or retrospective and do not isolate presidential causation; security and economic outcomes lack a complete target-period counterfactual analysis."]},{"question_id":"8B.8","answer":"The shard shows limited and contested adaptation. There were institutional responses such as creating extraordinary forensic mechanisms, changing investigative personnel, and using courts or audits to address failures. But repeated warnings and failures often did not produce effective correction: forensic and archive systems remained incomplete, corruption warnings accumulated without clear corrective action, autonomous-body appointments followed judicial compulsion, and Ayotzinapa investigators reported interference, noncooperation, and obstruction rather than course correction.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0018-E019","BATCH-0026-E003","BATCH-0026-E014","BATCH-0026-E020","BATCH-0030-E011","BATCH-0030-E012"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0018-E017","BATCH-0031-E019"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The shard lacks systematic audit-to-decision timelines showing whether the ruler personally reviewed failures, reallocated resources, or replaced implementers because of performance evidence."]},{"question_id":"8B.9","answer":"The ruler maintained and advanced selected objectives during institutional resistance and crises, particularly military expansion, infrastructure delivery, party succession, and contested reforms. Crisis and resistance management was mixed: courts invalidated or constrained reforms, opposition mobilized successfully, and the government sometimes complied with judicial orders. In Ayotzinapa, Otis response, and public-security controversies, the shard records delayed, incomplete, opaque, or allegedly protective responses, with no clear evidence that corrective action consistently preserved truth, accountability, or effective crisis outcomes.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0028-E003","BATCH-0026-E017","BATCH-0029-E003","BATCH-0031-E004","BATCH-0031-E013"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0018-E016","BATCH-0026-E012","BATCH-0026-E020","BATCH-0030-E012","BATCH-0031-E003"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The shard provides only partial operational information on federal disaster resources, crisis decisions, and the final consequences of institutional resistance."]},{"question_id":"8B.10","answer":"By the end of the supplied period, the ruler had converted substantial parts of his program into durable structures and practices, including social transfers, minimum-wage policy, expanded military roles, major infrastructure, and a dominant party network. Durability and achievement were mixed: some poverty and labor indicators improved, but economic and security goals remained weak, oversight and civilian capacity were impaired, projects were incomplete or costly, and several institutional changes were constitutionally contested or dependent on military and personal control. The shard therefore shows durable conversion in selected domains but not durable, broad achievement across the stated portfolio.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0026-E002","BATCH-0026-E004","BATCH-0026-E005","BATCH-0030-E004","BATCH-0031-E013","BATCH-0031-E016","BATCH-0032-E001"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0026-E008","BATCH-0029-E007","BATCH-0030-E005","BATCH-0031-E014","BATCH-0031-E015"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The period-end evidence is partly retrospective and includes post-2023 material; long-term durability, fiscal sustainability, and successor-period effects remain incompletely observed."]}],"cross_shard_cautions":["This shard mixes direct 2023 evidence with earlier program statements, lagged 2022 outcomes, and retrospective 2024-2026 analyses; target-period fit must be preserved item by item.","Several adverse claims are allegations, advocacy assessments, or analytical interpretations rather than final judicial findings; the records themselves identify those limits.","The material often documents inherited crises, subordinate or institutional conduct, external shocks, and national trends without isolating López Obrador's personal causal contribution.","No score is assigned."]}
